Aimed at strengthening Delhi’s firefighting and emergency rescue services, Chief Minister Rekha Gupta has approved the creation of 2,345 additional posts across various categories in the Delhi Fire Services (DFS), the CM’s Office (CMO) said on Saturday.
The Chief Minister said it was essential to strengthen the fire service in line with the city’s growing needs to ensure the safety of Delhi’s residents and save lives.
Under the restructuring, the number of posts will be increased across various ranks and categories, including Deputy Chief Fire Officer, Divisional Officer, Assistant Divisional Officer, Station Officer, Sub-Officer, Leading Fireman, Fire Operator, Peon and Gardener, as per the CMO.
“This will increase the availability of personnel at every level, from senior supervisory positions to frontline staff engaged in firefighting and rescue operations. It will also help streamline the department’s organisational structure, ensure better discharge of responsibilities at different levels and improve its efficiency during emergencies,” the CMO said in a statement.
The Chief Minister said that Delhi’s rapidly growing population, expanding urban areas, densely populated settlements, high-rise buildings, industrial establishments and complex infrastructure were creating new challenges for firefighting and emergency services.
“Every minute matters in the event of a fire or any other disaster. Adequately trained manpower, a strong leadership structure and the ability to respond quickly play a decisive role in protecting people and their property,” she said.
